- **Archive parent:** Double Decker
- **Builder:** Cicognani Engineering
- **Catalog type:** Overdrive
- **Identity:** Cicognani/Gurus 1959 Double Decker, a dual-channel tube overdrive inspired by late-1950s British amplifier circuits.

Historical documentation identifies the original 1959 Double Decker as a dual-channel overdrive designed by Guglielmo Cicognani for Gurus, with a circuit inspired by the classic British 1959 amplifier sound. Later Cicognani Engineering documentation describes the Speciale DD 1959 as the evolution of that same Double Decker project. [1][2]

- The original Italian-built Double Decker is documented in a metal enclosure, but no complete factory colorway sequence was established in the checked sources.

The original Double Decker is documented as a **two-channel** overdrive/preamplifier. Historical retailer documentation describes the channels as covering edge-of-breakup through higher-gain British lead sounds and supports use either into an amplifier or as a recording front end. [1]

Cicognani's later **Speciale DD 1959** is explicitly described as an evolution rather than a literal reissue. The later model adds a clean channel in Rec Out mode, an expanded gain structure on Channel 2, a redesigned effects loop, and more complete switching/control facilities. [2]

The original Double Decker is a tube/preamp design. Exact transistor part numbers were not established.

No exact-model diode specification was established.

The Double Decker is designed around British amplifier overdrive, with two channels covering edge-of-breakup through higher-gain lead territory. The design is intended to preserve touch dynamics and work either as an amp-front overdrive or as a recording preamp. [1]

1. Soundgas — Gurus 1959 Double Decker historical overview: https://soundgas.com/blogs/blog/gurus-1959-double-decker-a-pedalboard-essential
2. Cicognani Engineering / Speciale DD 1959 documentation: https://www.cicognani.eu/triple-decker/
